notes.decision: Initial ⲣⲉ taken as Lycopolitan reduction of circumstantial converter ⲉⲣⲉ-, governing the future ⲛⲁⲣ̄-ⲡⲍⲟⲩⲟ 'shall predominate.' This produces a temporal-circumstantial 'while...' clause introducing the chapter — the diagnostic condition (Fire of Darkness predominating) under which the body of the chapter is delivered.

Lexeme uncertain. Translated tentatively as 'the tree' on the basis of natural pairing with ⲡⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ 'the fruit.' Possibly a corrupt or scribal-variant spelling of ⲡϣⲏⲛ 'tree' or related to ⲧⲱϩⲛ 'mix' / ⲧⲱϩⲙ 'call.' Flagged for parallel attestations.

Lycopolitan negative existential construction. The form ⲕⲁⲟⲛ appears here to function as the existential element negated by ⲛⲉ-/ⲉⲛ; cf. parallel line 4 ⲛⲉⲕⲁⲟⲛ ⲟⲩⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲛⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'there is not a single man' and line 22 ⲉⲕⲁⲟⲛ ⲛⲣⲡⲏⲩⲉ 'there is not (a one of) the temples.' Translated 'it was not (such)' / 'there is not.'

Translated as 'this single Evil' — taking ⲁ-ϯ- as demonstrative-article complex (Lyc. variant of ⲧⲉⲓ-) + κακία 'evil/vice.' The 'three types' suggests three modes/forms in which this single Evil manifested and was purified. Alternative reading as Greek ἀκακία 'innocence' is possible but less likely given the verb ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲁⲥ 'they purified it' which points to evil-as-object-of-purification.

ⲙⲁⲛⲟⲩⲱⲥ̄ parsed as ⲙⲁ-ⲛ̄-ⲟⲩⲱⲥ̄ 'place of harvest,' from ⲱⲉⲥ 'reap' (already in glossary). The Fourth Work concerns the apostles purifying their threshing-floor / place of reaping — fitting the agricultural-eschatological frame.

Plural of ⲣⲡⲉ 'temple,' here 'the temples (of the upper place).' Distinct from ⲣⲣⲟ 'king' / ⲣⲡⲟ 'kingship.' The temples are 'united' (ⲉⲩⲧⲏⲧ) and 'completed forth' (ⲉⲩⲭⲏⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ) — the eschatological condition of the heavenly sanctuaries.

ⲫⲩⲥⲓ taken as Greek φύω 'grow, sprout, generate-by-nature' substantivized/verbalized — 'they shall sprout themselves.' The Seventh Work then concerns the souls' self-sprouting/regeneration at the cosmic rivers, leading to their arrival at their proper places and regions (line 25). Alternatively φύσει 'by nature.'

Reduplicated form likely from ⲭⲁⲗⲭ 'fashion together, mingle' (already in glossary), giving 'great fashionings' — i.e. final cosmological constructions/preparations paired with ⲥⲃⲧⲉⲩⲉ 'preparations.' Could alternatively be a joy-term (cf. ⲧⲉⲗⲏⲗ).
ⲧⲡ̄ taken as ⲧⲡⲉ 'head, beginning' — 'the head/beginning of the dissolution-forth of the world.' Marks the inception of cosmic dissolution as the contained item of the Ninth Work.
Form uncertain at line-end. Possibly ϩⲁⲣⲟⲕ 'before/unto you (sg.)' or 'alone, by yourself.' Translated tentatively 'to you'; flagged for review.
